tlv3501_delay_vs_load.assumes: that the switching table's own load is the left-hand end of this curve. The table states no capacitive load; the two agree near 4.5 to 4.7 ns typical, which is the reason for reading it that way.
tlv3501_delay_vs_load.document: TI TLV3501, TLV3502, SBOS321E (March 2005, revised April 2016), served by LCSC for C193413
tlv3501_delay_vs_load.shows: Figure 5: propagation delay against capacitive load at 20 mV overdrive. The fall curve starts at about 4.7 ns at 13 pF - close to the 4.5 ns the switching table gives as typical - and reaches about 8.2 ns at 100 pF, so the delay grows by roughly 40 ps for every picofarad hung on the output.
